description:
FILED s460ap (agent AP, round 17), with the measurement already taken -- this is
the price #891's fix pays, not a suspicion.

WHAT #891 DID.  %p-assign-snapshot's container arms (reference / blessed /
typeglob / dualvar) now return a FRESH box carrying the same inner value and
container flags, instead of the LIVE box.  They had to: keeping the live box
meant `($x,$y) = ($y,$x)` on references read $x back AFTER store 0 had
overwritten it.  One rule, one place, and it also fixed the two slice
self-swaps, because the slice arms of p-setf read the same rule through
%p-assign-snapshot-vector.

WHAT IT COSTS, MEASURED (best-of-3, startup subtracted, tools/bench-exec.pl
methodology).  The standard bench table does not move at all -- no row
list-assigns a reference:
    gcdrec    0.0939 -> 0.0913     arrfill   0.0717 -> 0.0712
    slices    0.2125 -> 0.2119     sliceasgn 0.0529 -> 0.0535
    ovlsub    0.1318 -> 0.1344     packunpk  4.379  -> 4.387
A deliberately worst-case micro-bench does:
    package Obj; sub add { my ($self,$x,$r) = @_; $self->{v} += $x + $r->[0] }
    4e6 method calls, one blessed box + one array-ref box per call
    base 2.31-0.18 = 2.13 s exec ; fixed 2.50-0.18 = 2.32 s exec  => +8.9 %
Two struct allocations per call, ~47 ns.  That is the shape real OO CPAN code
opens every method with, so it is worth recovering.

WHAT PERL DOES, AND WHY IT IS CHEAPER.  perl's pp_aassign copies the RHS to
mortals ONLY when the assignment is "common" -- the peephole optimizer sets
OPpASSIGN_COMMON_{RC1,SCALAR,AGG} when a variable can appear on both sides
(and perl 5.28+ adds a runtime refcount check for the rest).  `my ($self,$x) =
@_` is not common: the LHS are the sub's own fresh lexicals, so perl copies
nothing.

THE SHAPE THAT WOULD RECOVER IT (unimplemented, sized).  `p-list-=` is a MACRO
and knows its LHS target symbols at expansion time.  The hazard is exactly "a
src-vec element that IS (eq) a target box, read after that target was written",
so `assign-scalar` can, before storing into target T, replace every LATER
src-vec element that is `eq` T with %p-container-snapshot:
    (%p-protect-target T src-vec (1+ idx))
k targets x m src elements is a handful of EQ tests (3 targets / 3 sources =
~4.5) and ZERO allocations in the common case.  Then %p-assign-snapshot's
container arms could go back to returning the live box on the %p-flatten-list
(hot) path.

WHAT NOT TO RETRY, AND WHY (measured s460ap):
  - Do NOT narrow %p-assign-snapshot alone.  The p-setf array-slice and
    hash-slice arms read the SAME rule through %p-assign-snapshot-vector, and
    their targets are the container's own element boxes -- `@a[0,1] = @a[1,0]`
    with reference values regresses SILENTLY.  Whatever narrows the hot path
    must leave the slice arms copying (they are cold and already allocate
    lazily), or give them their own exact target check.
  - Do NOT try to hand box-set a bare aggregate instead of a box: box-set's
    "raw adjustable vector / hash-table in a scalar assignment becomes its
    COUNT" rule fires on a non-box value, so an array ref handed over bare
    becomes an integer.
  - A COMPILE-TIME-only commonality test is not sufficient on its own:
    `our ($p,$q); sub f { ($p,$q) = @_ } f($q,$p)` puts the caller's boxes in
    @_ and the RHS form mentions neither $p nor $q.  The eq-scan above is a
    RUNTIME test and does not have this hole.

BAR: Pl/t/aassign-01.t rows 37-40 unchanged (they are #891's guard, positives
plus the identity/class/dualvar/glob/refaliasing inverse), perl-tests/
multideref.t row 42 "OA_DANGEROUS b" still passing, the full sweep, and the
micro-bench above back at ~2.13 s exec.


SHIPPED s461aq (round 18), but NOT in the shape the task sketched â and the
difference IS the finding.

WHAT SHIPPED: `%p-flatten-list` takes the assignment's TARGET BOXES (a
DYNAMIC-EXTENT list built by the p-list-= macro, so the fast path allocates
nothing at all) and its leaf arm keeps a container-valued element LIVE unless
that element IS one of the targets â perl's OPpASSIGN_COMMON rule, asked per
element, ON THE WALK THAT ALREADY HAS THE ELEMENT IN HAND.  The gate is the
all-scalar LHS (every element a plain `$` symbol, k <= 8); a REF-WRAPPER box
is still copied (box-set stores such a box by IDENTITY).  `%p-in-targets-p`
is the inlined eq scan.

WHY NOT THE TASK'S SHAPE â MEASURED, 4e6 OO method entries, min of 5,
interleaved on one machine:
    base (snapshot always)                        1.811 s
    keep-container, NO commonality check (unsafe) 1.700 s   (-6.1 %)
    the task's %p-protect-target, per target      1.810 s   (+0.0 %)
    one INLINE pass over src-vec, all targets     1.822 s   (+0.6 %)
    SHIPPED (the test rides the flattener's walk) 1.702 s   (-5.0 %)
The two allocations are worth 6 %; ANY extra pass over the source vector
costs the same 6 %, because that vector is ADJUSTABLE and every `aref` on it
is a generic call (~7 ns) â filed as task #923.  So the rule is: the
commonality test must not add a traversal.  Consing per 1e6 calls:
1685.5 MB -> 1567.1 MB (two p-boxes per call, ~118 bytes).

BARS: the 16-shape swap battery vs perl 5.40.3 (plain scalars, ARRAY / HASH /
CODE refs, blessed, globs and glob refs, dualvars incl. $!, \-wrappers, the
mixed `($x,$y)=($x->{a},$x)`, the runtime-common `our ($p,$q); sub f {
($p,$q)=@_ } f($q,$p)` that no compile-time name test can see, same box
twice, self-assign, @_ aliasing, identity+class through @_) â byte-identical.
Pl/t/aassign-01.t 40 -> 42 rows, INVERSE-GUARDED: with the commonality test
removed, rows 37-38 (#891's) and 41-42 (the new ones) all fail.
perl-tests/multideref.t row 42 "OA_DANGEROUS b" still passing.  Gate PASS
191/6462; full sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18342 (+0).
subject: p-list-= allocates a container-box copy per REFERENCE element; perl only copies when the assignment is COMMON (#891's measured price, ~9% on OO method entry)
